column2: summary

HarnessSelfVerificationTest found nothingArrivedFor() could pass without ever observing a message that was actually present mid-window; TC-32's absence assertion rested entirely on it and could not have failed before it was strengthened to sample throughout the window and judge absence per booking id. Commit 1bfe9b6.

TC-39 asserted on a drain() snapshot taken immediately after publishing instead of polling until both outputs for the shared key had arrived, so the ordering scenario raced the service and failed for a reason that looked like an ordering defect and was a missing wait in the suite. Commit 3992565.

EndToEndSmokeTest and HarnessSelfVerificationTest called TestConfig.load("local") with the profile hardcoded instead of TestConfig.load(), so -Dsuite.env=ci was ignored and both tests looked for the service jar at a local-only path that does not exist on a CI runner; CI could never pass regardless of what else was fixed. Commit e7aa8a6.

The CI workflow's credential check read $SERVICE_SSH_KEY while the env block still exported the token name it replaced, SERVICE_TOKEN, so the variable was never set and the integration jobs skipped despite the secret existing on the repository -- a green, uninformative run with the wrong stated reason. Commit fab2bee.

Surefire's default include pattern named only **/RunCucumberTest.java, a class that did not exist yet, so `mvn test` ran zero tests and reported BUILD SUCCESS -- a green build testing nothing, and one that would have permanently excluded the suite's own plain-JUnit helper tests as well. Commit fbd2909.

RunCucumberTest carried no JUnit tag, so an untagged `mvn test` included it and it silently used whatever Kafka broker happened to be running locally -- green with a broker present, but would fail unpredictably on a runner with none, with no signal that the default build was ever meant to need one. Commit 3913e77.

Step definitions appended the schema version a second time when validating against a schema named as published (e.g. "booking-enriched-v1"), looking up "booking-enriched-v1-v1" and failing six schema-contract scenarios that were otherwise correctly implemented. Commit 99342dd.

TC-38's route-matching step compared the outcome "ENRICHED" (as given in the Examples table) against the lower-case topic name, fell through to the flagged branch, and waited the full poll timeout for a message that was never coming on that topic. Commit 99342dd.

The step "its origin is X and its destination is Y", used as setup before a booking is published in TC-26, TC-72, TC-73 and TC-74, was implemented as a Then instead of a Given, so it ran as an assertion during setup and failed looking for an output message that could not exist yet. Reclassified as a Given that amends the staged booking. Commit 99342dd.

TC-51 stages a malformed payload and a valid booking in two separate Given steps sharing one staging slot; the second Given overwrote the first, so the scenario published the booking twice and never actually sent a malformed payload, despite the assertion appearing to pass. Raw and booking payloads now use separate slots. Commit 99342dd.

Mutation 3 (docs/MUTATION_CHECK.md: flagged bookings also published to the enriched topic) was run against a mutated service and showed TC-42 does not fail: a flagged message that also lands on booking.enriched still passes validation against the booking-enriched-v1 schema, so the "two independent mechanisms" enforcing routing exclusivity claimed by TEST_SUITE_SPEC.md section 13.6 and the schema_contract.feature TC-42 comment do not actually both hold -- only TC-32's behavioural check does. Not yet reflected back into docs/MUTATION_CHECK.md's own (blank) results table.
